body.input: Which companies opened an office in Germany in 2026?

response.content:
Based on available reporting, here are companies that opened an office or established a new presence in Germany in 2026:

1. **WB Group** (Poland) — Opened a representative office in Berlin on November 10, 2026, and established **WB Germany GmbH**. The Polish defense technology company (drones, communication systems, battlefield management) also acquired a German technology company, reportedly Regensburg-based Smoto. The Berlin office serves as a contact point for the Bundeswehr, industry partners, and research organizations.

2. **Rheinmetall** — Announced in August 2026 the development of a new logistics and technology center at Kassel Airport in Calden (North Hesse), with investment in the hundreds of millions of euros, including plans for a drone test center. The company also invested nearly €500 million in a new ammunition production facility in Unterlüß, Lower Saxony.

3. **KNDS** — Converting a former Alstom rail factory in Görlitz into a defense manufacturing site, with over half of its 70,000 m² of production space converted and approximately 400 employees expected by end of 2026.

4. **digiLab** (UK) — Joined the UK Tech Accelerator in Germany and opened a new office in **Stuttgart**, expanding its market presence in Europe as an AI company focused on fusion technology and other sectors.

5. **MGI Tech** — Expanded its European footprint with a new office opening in Germany.

6. **Evonik** — Invested €52 million to expand its silicone platform at its Essen Goldschmidtstrasse site, including construction of a new production plant and tank farm.

7. **Urenco** (UK) — Announced plans to invest €1 billion to expand its site in Gronau, Germany (2025–2035).

The defense sector was a particularly strong driver of new office and facility openings in Germany in 2026, with German defense expenditures projected to reach €108 billion (2.5% of GDP) in 2026.

*Note: This list reflects publicly reported openings and may not be exhaustive.*

# WB Group Opens Berlin Office and Expands in Germany

Opening of the Berlin office of WB Group

Opening of the Berlin office of WB Group - © WB Group (LinkedIn) [...] Company founder Piotr Wojciechowski described Germany and Poland as key partners in strengthening European security. WB Group sees itself as an industrial bridge between both countries and aims to deepen cooperation following the German Polish defense agreement signed in June 2026.

The Berlin opening also reflects increasing international interest in Germany's defense sector. During the launch event, Polish Deputy Foreign Minister Marcin Bosacki said he expects further investments and acquisitions by companies from Poland and other Central and Eastern European countries.

Thinking about launching a business, setting up premises, or creating partnerships in Berlin?  
We invite you to contact us.  
Our team is ready to help you with our free consultation services.

 Previous News [...] WB Group develops and manufactures drones, communication systems and battlefield management technologies. The privately owned company employs more than 3,000 people, including around 1,500 researchers and developers. Current development work focuses on faster drones, reduced signatures, improved protection against countermeasures and higher levels of autonomy.

The new Berlin office is intended to serve as a contact point for industry partners, government institutions, the Bundeswehr, research organizations and defense technology companies. The company also plans to expand existing partnerships with German firms, including cooperation in vehicle integration, unmanned ground systems and networked operational capabilities.

context.content:
Polish defense technology company WB Group has opened a representative office in Berlin and established WB Germany GmbH, expanding its industrial presence in Europe's largest economy.

The new German subsidiary was formally presented on November 10, 2026. The expansion includes a technology business in Bavaria and the acquisition of an existing German company, as WB Group seeks closer cooperation with German manufacturers, military customers and research institutions.

According to German defense publication hartpunkt, WB Group has already acquired a company in southern Germany but has not publicly confirmed its identity. German business reporting has identified Regensburg-based Smoto, a supplier of electric propulsion technology for drones, as the possible acquisition target. [...] In September 2026, WB Group demonstrated its Gladius strike system during Bundeswehr trials. The company has reported favorable results, although its claims regarding accuracy and resistance to electronic warfare have not been independently verified by AdriaDefense.

The Berlin expansion adds another dimension to WB Group's international growth. As AdriaDefense recently reported, the Polish company is also exploring a potential stock market listing in 2027 at a valuation reportedly reaching €7 billion.

Its German presence could strengthen the company's position in future Bundeswehr procurement programs while allowing it to combine Polish-developed technologies with German industrial capabilities. [...] AdriaDefense

One of the clearest examples is in Unterlüß, Lower Saxony, where Rheinmetall invested nearly €500 million in a new ammunition production facility at its existing site. The plant can produce up to 350,000 artillery shells annually once fully ramped.

A second major investment is taking shape in North Hesse. Rheinmetall announced in August 2026 that it will develop a new logistics and technology center at Kassel Airport in Calden. The investment is in the hundreds of millions of euros and includes a logistics center, as well as plans for a drone test center. [...] Photo courtesy of Rheinmetall

A Faster Path to Production  
In Görlitz, KNDS is converting a former Alstom rail factory into a defense manufacturing site. Since acquiring the site in February 2025, the company has converted more than half of its 70,000 square meters (753,000 sq. ft.) of production space and expects to employ about 400 people there by the end of 2026.

The site offered KNDS something difficult to reproduce quickly through a greenfield project: an existing workforce with extensive metalworking experience.

“People who have built bodies for double-deck coaches know how to weld, assemble and inspect large, complex steel structures to strict quality standards,” says a KNDS spokesperson. “That know-how cannot be bought off the shelf.” [...] by Savannah Yawn

Germany’s defense-industrial expansion is creating a new wave of manufacturing investment across the country. German defense expenditures rose from €52.4 billion in 2021 to €107 billion in 2025 and are projected to reach €108 billion, or 2.5% of GDP, in 2026, according to Germany Trade & Invest.

But Germany is not building that capacity from a blank slate.

“Germany combines rising demand with one of Europe’s deepest industrial and innovation bases,” says Christoph Mester, Germany Trade & Invest defense expert. “This creates credible entry opportunities for established defense companies, dual-use technology providers and specialized suppliers seeking to scale in Europe.”

# Evonik invests €52 million to expand silicone platform in Essen [...] Essen, Germany. Evonik has invested €52 million in expanding its silicone platform at the Essen Goldschmidtstrasse site in Germany. The investment included the construction of a new production plant and a large tank farm. The new facility increases production capacity for organomodified silicones, a key product group within Evonik’s international silicone network. These tailored silicone additives are used in applications including polyurethane foams for insulation materials, mattresses or automotive seating, as well as in adhesives, coatings and personal care products.
